# Background

The gene ids are present in a couple of different forms. We want to make a table mapping all id forms to each other. The ids are in the following forms.

1. In the gtf, in the db_xref attribute, we have gene_ids in the form `GeneID:1234567`, `mirBase:1234567`, etc.
2. In the gene info table I donwloaded from NCBI Gene database, the ids are in the form `1234567`
3. In KEGG Genome database, they are in the form `cin:1234567`


# Setup
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# knitr options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = 300, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
library(here)

genomedir <- here("species/crob/genome/refseq_KH/")
```

# Data
## Full data
```{r, message=FALSE}
gtf <- read_tsv(here(genomedir, "results/gtf/gtf_fixed_parsed.tsv"), 
                col_types = cols(
                  .default = col_character(),
                  start = col_double(),
                  end = col_double(),
                  width = col_double(),
                  exon_number = col_double()
                ))

ncbi <- read_tsv(here(genomedir, "results/genes/ncbi-genes-table.tsv"))
```

## Get rid of unnecessary columns and rows
```{r}
gtf_ids <- gtf %>% 
  filter(type == "gene") %>% 
  select(gene_id, symbol) %>% 
  distinct()

ncbi_ids <- ncbi %>% 
  select(ncbi_gene_id, symbol) %>% 
  distinct()
```

# Process GTF gene ids
All gene ids come from NCBI Gene database
```{r}
gtf_ids %>% 
  separate(gene_id, into = c("db", "id"), sep = ":") %>% 
  count(db)
```

```{r}
gtf_ids <- gtf_ids %>% 
  separate(gene_id, into = c("db", "ncbi_gene_id"), sep = ":", remove = FALSE)

```

# Missing genes from GTF and NCBI gene table

Some gene ids from the GTF file are missing in the NCBI gene table and vice versa. We need to figure out why this happens and what these genes are. 

## Missing from GTF but present in NCBI gene table

```{r}
all(ncbi_ids$ncbi_gene_id %in% gtf_ids$ncbi_gene_id)
```

```{r}
ncbi_ids %>% 
  filter(!(ncbi_gene_id %in% gtf_ids$ncbi_gene_id)) %>% 
  arrange(symbol) %>% 
  print(n = 30)
```

There are 170 gene ids that are present in the NCBI gene table but are absent from the GTF file. Some of these seems to be important genes, like `hnf4`. But, we can see that the symbol `hnf4` is present in the GTF file, but with another gene id. 

```{r}
gtf_ids %>% 
  filter(str_detect(symbol, "hnf4")) 
```

If we look for the symbol `hnf4` in the ncbi table, we see that this symbol is associated with two different gene ids. 

```{r}
ncbi_ids %>% 
  filter(symbol == "hnf4")
```

If we look up these two ids on NCBI Gene database (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/?term=778645 and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/?term=780712) we can see that gene id 780712 is not present in the current annotation release. It's probably been replaced by 778645. 

This suggests that we need not worry about the genes that missing from the GTF file but are present in the NCBI gene table. These genes are likely outdated annotations that have been replaced. In a few cases that I manually looked up, in all cases, those genes were stil present in the GTF file but with a different gene id. For example `foxl2` is missing from GTF, but `foxL` is present, which is a synonym for `foxl2`. 

## Missing from NCBI gene table but present in GTF
```{r}
gtf_ids %>% 
  filter(!(ncbi_gene_id %in% ncbi_ids$ncbi_gene_id))
```

There are 39 gene ids present in the GTF file but are missing from the NCBI gene table. These are all mitochondrial genes since they are from the mitochondrial genome seq `NC_017929.1`

```{r}
gtf %>% 
  filter(type == "gene") %>% 
  separate(gene_id, into = c("db", "id"), sep = ":") %>% 
  filter(db == "ncbi") %>% 
  filter(!(id %in% ncbi_ids$ncbi_gene_id)) %>% 
  pull(seqnames) %>% 
  unique()
```

This suggests that we also don't have to worry about this set of genes -- it only means that the NCBI gene table we donwloaded doesn't include the mitochondrial genes. 

# Conclusion
We will only save the gene ids from the GTF file:

1. it contains the mitochondrial genes unlike the NCBI gene table
2. NCBI gene table contains some genes that have been replaced by other annotations, so we don't want them. 
3. The `gtf_id` object now contains the gene ids in all the relevant fornmats. 

# write gene ids to file
```{r}
write_tsv(gtf_ids, here(genomedir, "results/genes/gene-ids.tsv"))
```
